authority: experiment-owner direction to deepen the thinnest single-replicate claims
finding: After the shared OpenAI access token expired, exactly one lane can succeed. That lane refreshes the token inside its ephemeral copy of the credential, the refreshed tokens are discarded with the lane, and the source file keeps a refresh token that has now been consumed. Every later lane copies that stale refresh token and is rejected with 401.

evidence.provider_error: codex_login::auth::manager: Failed to refresh token: 401 Unauthorized -- 'Your refresh token has already been used to generate a new access token. Please try signing in again.'

source_credential_state.note: The file has not been written since 2026-09-18, so no lane has ever persisted a refreshed token back to it.

evidence.mechanism_in_code: scripts/run_codex_fixture_evaluation.py copies the credential into the lane home with shutil.copy2 and records auth_materialization as copy-ephemeral. The copy is one-way by design, which is correct for credential hygiene and has the side effect that a refresh performed inside a lane is never durable.
sequence_observed: 2026-09-29 token-savior-fastify-r1 runs, refreshes inside its ephemeral copy, completes 6/6, discards the new tokens
2026-09-29T23:17Z tokenjuice-fastify-r1 copies the same now-consumed refresh token and fails 401 on task-01

why_this_was_not_seen_earlier: The access token was valid from 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-28, so no lane in that window needed to refresh. Every OpenAI-provider failure before the expiry had a different cause and is receipted separately: quota exhaustion on 09-22 and 09-23, and unexplained provider slowness with no errors on 09-24 through 09-26.
affected: All OpenAI-provider lanes, both the codex-cli and opencode-cli runtimes, since they share this credential. Claude Code lanes are unaffected; they use a separate Anthropic credential and have been completing normally, including two on 09-28 and 09-29.

disclosed_spend.note: No provider turn completed. task-01 was attempted and exited 1 on the auth failure; the run record carries no cumulative usage and the retained diff is 132 bytes. Disclosed as effectively zero rather than as a measured spend.
disclosed_spend.ingress: The lane was additionally refused by strict compact artifact ingress validation, which is the correct handling of a session carrying no usable telemetry.

required_to_unblock: Re-authenticate the OpenAI/Codex account so /opt/data/home/.codex/auth.json holds a fresh access token and an unused refresh token. This needs an interactive sign-in and cannot be done from here.
durable_fix_worth_considering: Persist a refreshed credential back to the source home after a lane completes, or refresh once in the controller before each launch rather than letting each lane refresh independently. Either removes the one-lane-per-expiry ceiling. Both touch credential handling, so neither is attempted here without direction.

resolved_20261002.finding: The account had been re-authenticated on 2026-09-29T14:44:51Z, but into /opt/data/auth.json, a multi-provider credential pool, rather than the flat /opt/data/home/.codex/auth.json that DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODEX_HOME points the runner at. The runner kept reading the stale file and every OpenAI lane stayed blocked for three days after the credential was actually fixed.
resolved_20261002.independent_confirmation_of_the_diagnosi: That pool file records last_auth_error {'code': 'refresh_token_reused', 'message': 'Codex refresh token was already consumed by ano...'}, which is the same single-use-refresh failure diagnosed here from the lane side on 09-29.
resolved_20261002.action: Materialised the pool's openai-codex entry into the flat format the runner reads: auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY, tokens and last_refresh, with the prior file preserved at auth.json.bak-20261002 and mode 600. The tokens object was byte-identical in shape, so this is a reformat rather than a credential change.
resolved_20261002.verified: Access token valid to 2026-10-09T14:44:51Z. Throughput probe returns 322 words in 10s at 32.2 words/s.
resolved_20261002.standing_risk_unchanged: This does not fix the underlying defect. The lane copy is still one-way, so when this token expires on 10-09 the same one-lane-per-expiry behaviour returns unless a refreshed credential is persisted back to the source or refreshed once in the controller before launch.
resolved_20261002.operational_note: Two credential locations now exist on this machine for the same account. Whichever is authoritative should be the one DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODEX_HOME reads, or the runner should learn the pool format; otherwise a future re-authentication can again appear to have no effect.
